outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Low-Precision Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter provides the motivation for 1-bit LLMs, discussing the computational and environmental costs of traditional full-precision models and the existing landscape of quantization.
subtopics: The growth of LLMs and the 'Memory Wall'
Energy consumption and environmental impact of floating-point operations
Introduction to precision: FP16, BF16, and the move toward low-bit representations
Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) vs. Training from Scratch
Limitations of current 4-bit and 8-bit quantization methods

outline.chapter_title: Foundations of BitNet and the 1-bit Paradigm
outline.description: An exploration of the fundamental shift from floating-point matrix multiplication to integer addition, introducing the core concepts of the BitNet architecture.
subtopics: The computational cost of nn.Linear in Transformers
BitLinear: Replacing floating-point multiplication with integer addition
Theoretical energy savings of additive computation
Memory bandwidth bottlenecks: DRAM vs. SRAM
The conceptual transition from binary (1-bit) to ternary (1.58-bit) weights

outline.description: A detailed technical explanation of the BitNet b1.58 variant, focusing on the ternary weight system and the specific quantization functions used.
subtopics: Understanding the Ternary Set: {-1, 0, 1}
Why 1.58 bits? (The mathematics of log2(3))
The Absmean Quantization Function: Scaling and Rounding
The RoundClip mechanism for weight constraint
Activation Quantization: Per-token scaling to [-Qb, Qb]
Feature Filtering: The role of the '0' weight in model capability

outline.description: This chapter explains how BitNet b1.58 is built upon the LLaMA architecture to ensure compatibility with modern open-source ecosystems.
subtopics: The LLaMA backbone: A review of the de-facto standard
RMSNorm (Root Mean Square Layer Normalization)
SwiGLU activation functions
Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE)
Integration with open-source frameworks: HuggingFace, vLLM, and llama.cpp

outline.description: An analysis of the experimental results, comparing BitNet b1.58 against full-precision baselines across various model sizes and tasks.
subtopics: Evaluation Metrics: Perplexity and Zero-Shot Accuracy
The '3B Threshold': When 1.58-bit models match FP16 performance
Comparative analysis on RedPajama and WikiText2 datasets
End-task performance: ARC, Hellaswag, and Winogrande
Scaling the model: From 3B to 70B parameters

outline.description: A comprehensive look at the hardware-level advantages of BitNet b1.58, including latency, memory footprint, and energy consumption.
subtopics: GPU Memory Consumption and Latency Reductions
Analyzing Throughput: Batch size increases and pipeline parallelism
The Arithmetic Energy Model: FP16 vs. INT8 addition
The New Scaling Law: Equivalent performance across precision levels (e.g., BitNet 70B vs. FP16 13B)
Generalization capabilities with large-scale training (2T tokens)

outline.description: The final chapter discusses the broader implications of 1-bit LLMs, including their application to Mixture-of-Experts, long-context windows, and specialized hardware.
subtopics: 1-bit Mixture-of-Experts (MoE): Reducing communication overhead
Native support for long sequences: Reducing KV cache precision
Edge and Mobile Deployment: CPU-friendly LLMs
The call for specialized 1-bit hardware: Moving beyond GPUs to LPUs
Summary of the shift toward the 1-bit era
